eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices a 21°C high at 34.5% implied probability for São Paulo on May 11, reflecting INMET's May 4–11 weekly outlook of stable Southeast weather with dropping temperatures over the weekend from an incoming cooler air mass, low cloudiness, and isolated weak showers in southern areas that cap daytime heating. Recent daily observations confirm this cooling trend amid autumnal patterns, where May climatological highs average 23°C but current upper-level ridging favors milder maxima around 20–22°C. High uncertainty stems from variable cloud cover and southerly winds influencing convective timing—clearer skies could push toward 23°C (8.3%), while thicker overcast might drop to 19°C (5.0%)—with INMET's next 12Z model run and hourly station data at key sites like Congonhas pivotal before resolution.

Differentiating factors include model divergences on afternoon clearing—ECMWF slightly warmer, GFS cooler—and minor variations in surface observations; overnight updates may shift odds before DWD's official Munich station reading resolves the market. Historical May 11 averages hover near 17°C, underscoring the narrow uncertainty range.

eventMetadata.context_description: ECMWF and GFS model ensembles, as aggregated by Weather Underground and AccuWeather, converge on a high temperature of 20–22°C for Warsaw on May 11 under overcast skies and a 70–90% chance of afternoon showers from a weakening high-pressure ridge over Central Europe, driving trader consensus with 22°C at 44.5% implied probability, 23°C at 31%, and 21°C at 18%. Recent IMGW observations highlight spring variability—27°C peaks early last week, cooling to 13–14°C on May 8 amid clouds, and yesterday's 19°C high—against May climatological averages near 19°C, supporting the tight clustering while allowing for shower-induced fluctuations. Monitor today's IMGW synoptic updates and ECMWF 12z run for refinements ahead of official Warsaw station measurements resolving the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket clusters around 31°C (45.5%) and 32°C (32.0%) for Beijing's highest temperature on May 11, driven by the China Meteorological Administration's (CMA) latest forecast of a 30°C peak under sunny-to-cloudy skies and light southeast winds, amid North China's first heat wave of 2026. Recent observations confirm May 10 highs surpassing 30.5°C by late afternoon despite partial cloud cover, signaling persistent warm air advection following cooler May 9 readings below 22°C and a 30°C peak on May 5. This exceeds mid-May climatological averages of 27–28°C, with numerical weather prediction models like ECMWF hinting at possible 1–2°C upside from high pressure subsidence. Overnight forecast updates from CMA stations will clarify before official resolution at Beijing Capital International Airport.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket closely splits between 34°C (49.5%) and 33°C (40.0%) for Jakarta's highest temperature on May 11, reflecting uncertainty in how light rain and cloud cover—forecast by BMKG—will cap daytime heating amid an ongoing hot spell. AccuWeather models align nearer 33°C (92°F), with key variables including morning cloud timing and sea breeze moderation; final BMKG observations will resolve post-midnight May 12. Historical May averages hover at 32°C, but recent extremes underscore forecast divergence.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in National Weather Service and ensemble model forecasts for Panama City, Florida's highest temperature on May 12, with implied probabilities clustered around 30–33°C (86–91°F) outcomes at 23–29%, driven by a strengthening subtropical high pressure ridge promoting subsidence and warmer 850 mb temperatures aloft. Recent observations through May 9–10 show highs recovering to 80–82°F (27–28°C) after cloudy showers suppressed peaks, aligning with mid-May climatological averages of 84°F (29°C) but with upside potential from sunnier skies and light winds. Differentiating factors include Gulf sea breeze timing, which could enhance onshore flow and convection to cap highs at 30°C, versus delayed inland push allowing 32–33°C peaks; inherent model spread in GFS (hotter bias) versus ECMWF adds volatility. Watch 12Z updates Tuesday for refined guidance ahead of resolution.

Persistent dry season subsidence and urban heat island effects in central Manila, including Quezon City observatory readings, elevate implied probabilities above baseline May averages of 33–34°C, while low rain chances (20–40%) limit cooling. ENSO-neutral conditions prevail, but potential early El Niño signals could amplify heat; key differentiators include sea breeze timing and thunderstorm coverage, with new PAGASA bulletins expected daily resolving uncertainties before the 24-hour observation window.
